findings.title: A retry bypasses the device limit after the first rejection
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` adds the device ID to the local cache before persisting it and does not evict the entry when persistence fails. With this new error propagation, the first request for an over-limit device is rejected, but subsequent requests with the same ID hit the cache and return successfully without checking the limit. A retry can therefore authenticate despite the configured cap for the cache TTL. Only cache the ID after a successful store operation, or remove it on failure.

findings.title: Concurrent registrations can exceed the configured limit
findings.body: The device count check and the subsequent insert are separate database operations with no reservation or lock. Concurrent requests for different device IDs can both observe a count below the limit and both insert, leaving the database above the configured cap. This can also happen across Grafana instances sharing the database. Enforce the cap atomically across the count-and-insert operation.

findings.title: A no-op update can reject an existing device on MySQL
findings.body: This treats zero affected rows as proof that the device is absent. MySQL normally reports changed rows, not matched rows, so an update that matches an existing device but changes no values can return zero. Since MySQL timestamps are stored at second precision, a request on another instance in the same second with the same IP and user agent can leave every updated column unchanged and incorrectly return `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, rejecting an already-registered device when the cap is full. Check whether the row exists independently of whether the update changed it, or otherwise handle the database's matched-row semantics.

findings.title: The new configuration option is not documented
findings.body: This introduces `auth.anonymous.device_limit`, but the PR does not add it to the shipped configuration reference or defaults documentation. Operators cannot discover the setting or learn its default and behavior, making the feature difficult to configure reliably.
